title.narrative: Emergency Cholera Response through Enhanced WASH Services in Kassala State, Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtSamaritan's Purse (SP) is undertaking a comprehensive project in Kassala State to combat cholera and other rainy season diseases affecting vulnerable internally displaced people (IDPs) across 16 gathering sites and host communities. The core strategy involves implementing sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions with significant community involvement. This multifaceted approach aims to tackle the causes of disease transmission, ultimately leading to a substantial reduction in cholera incidence and an improvement in the overall health and well-being of the targeted populations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe immediate humanitarian response by SP will focus on providing critical WASH assistance to 5,000 individuals severely impacted by the recent cholera outbreak in the localities of Elgirba, West Kassala, and New Halfa. Recognizing the urgent needs of IDP families and those with limited access to essential resources, the intervention will ensure the delivery of vital aid to alleviate suffering and prevent further spread of the disease within these highly affected areas.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe WASH intervention encompasses a range of activities Such as, distribution of 1,000 hygiene and dignity kits to as many households, safe drinking water will be provided to 1,845 individuals through water trucking. To address sanitation infrastructure deficits, the project includes the construction of 10 new latrines and the rehabilitation of 10 semi-permanent ones, alongside the establishment of 6 shower and sanitation facilities, collectively serving approximately 4,750 beneficiaries. Proper waste management will be facilitated through desludging services.ltbrgtBeyond the crucial infrastructure improvements, the project places a strong emphasis on community health and hygiene promotion. Educational activities will reach 5,000 individuals, promoting essential practices such as handwashing and safe food handling. The installation of 6 communal shower stations and water chlorination will further support these efforts. Looking ahead, a post-rainy season spray campaign will target flies to mitigate cholera transmission. Collaboration with the State Ministry of Health is integral to integrating effective practices into long-term WASH strategies. Additionally, 90 cleaning campaigns and improved solid waste management will be implemented in IDP sites, with the strategic use of calcium oxide and Aqua Reslin in the cholera response.ltbrgtThe anticipated outcomes of this comprehensive project are significant. Access to clean water will be restored for 1,845 individuals, reducing the burden of long-distance water collection. Sanitation coverage in targeted communities will improve, leading to enhanced hygiene standards in gathering sites and public spaces. A key objective is to increase the proportion of community members demonstrating proper handwashing and hygiene techniques to 95%. Overall sanitation and hygiene practices are expected to improve, consequently lowering the risk of WASH-related diseases and enhancing public health for 5,000 individuals. Furthermore, increased access to hygiene products will contribute to infection prevention and promote overall health for 1,000 HHs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis vital intervention is a collaborative effort, involving local authorities, community leaders, line ministries, local non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) partners. By fostering strong partnerships, the project aims to ensure a timely and efficient response that is both sustainable and addresses immediate needs while laying the groundwork for long-term recovery. Continuous monitoring in initial intervention areas will be crucial to maintaining zero reported cholera cases and preventing recurrence. Furthermore, upcoming rainy season WASH interventions will include increased hygiene promotion through house-to-house visits, community cleaning campaigns, water quality monitoring, and the establishment of Water User Committees for the management of water sources.ltbrgtlt/pgt
